note: EXAMPLE ONLY -- placeholder tokens. The real file is PRIVATE and lives outside this repository, because the tokens it carries name a specific deployment environment and R-LOC-03 forbids committing operator-specific knowledge here. tests/_portability_gate.py resolves it at runtime, in order, from: $AGENTWARE_PORTABILITY_NEEDLES, then <knowledge-dir>/config/portability-needles.json, then <workspace>/.aw-migration-safety/portability-needles.json. When none exists the gate reports the 'environment' class as 'unavailable' -- it never reads as a clean pass. The zero-tolerance 'operator_product' class is NOT configurable here: it is defined in code so it cannot be weakened, redefined or disabled from outside the repository, and a needle in this file claiming that class is a schema violation.

needles.hint: an internal hostname or remote URL that must not ship
match: 'word' when the token is also an ordinary English word, so only whole-token occurrences fire
a vendor name; 'exempt' lists path prefixes where a hit is a known false positive
needles.reason: state WHY each exemption exists -- a path-scoped exemption with no reason is indistinguishable from a silent allowlist. Exemptions are legal for this class only.

needles.hint: a real person's corporate alias. Test FIXTURES are where these hide: an org/team suite seeds handles, curator rosters and per-user fleet shards, and every one of them is a real name unless someone neutralised it. Needle the alias so the gate proves the neutralisation instead of a reviewer eyeballing it.

an internal team or product key used as a fixture team name. Prefer a COMPOUND key here: a single-word team name that is also ordinary English cannot be needled without firing on unrelated prose (a 'metrics' team would hit every metrics comment in the tree), so neutralise those in the fixtures and record the reason, rather than adding a needle that must then be exempted everywhere it fires.
